finding.claim: Address6.isLinkLocal() returns false for fe80::/10 addresses with nonzero bits 10-63 (e.g. fe80:0:0:1::1), while getType() and getScope() classify the same address as link-local.
finding.source: Attacker-chosen IPv6 literal such as fe80:0:0:1::1 supplied as untrusted input
finding.sink: isLinkLocal() used as a trust-boundary deny check (SSRF filter) by the caller

trace.note: isLinkLocal(); embeddedIPv4() is null for this address
compares getBitsBase2(0,64) to an exact string: fe80 prefix then 54 zeros, so any nonzero bit in 10-63 fails
getType() uses isHostInSubnet('fe80::/10') and returns 'Link-local unicast' for the same address
getScope() maps 'Link-local unicast' to 'Link local'

finding.guards_checked: embeddedIPv4 short-circuit (not applicable: no mapped or NAT64 prefix). No other guard. Whether the OS treats such an address as on-link was not verified by execution.

finding.claim: Unspecified addresses 0.0.0.0 and :: are not matched by isPrivate(), isLoopback() or isLinkLocal() on either family, although the library documents these classifiers as SSRF trust-boundary checks.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled URL host such as http://0.0.0.0/ or http://[::]/
finding.sink: Outbound request in an application whose deny-list uses isPrivate/isLoopback/isLinkLocal but not isUnspecified

trace.note: Address4.isPrivate() checks only 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16
isLoopback() checks 127/8 only
isLinkLocal() checks 169.254/16 only
0.0.0.0 is reported only by isUnspecified()
Address6.isPrivate() on :: returns false, same gap
:: is reported only by isUnspecified()

finding.guards_checked: isUnspecified() exists and is correct, but callers must remember to call it. Kernel behaviour for 0.0.0.0 and :: was not verified here.

finding.claim: isInSubnet() is containment-based and returns false when the caller's prefix is shorter than the range's, so an attacker-chosen small suffix hides an address that isHostInSubnet() and isPrivate() both classify as private.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied IPv4 or IPv6 literal with a short CIDR suffix, e.g. 10.1.2.3/7
finding.sink: Application deny-check using isInSubnet(10.0.0.0/8), then a request to correctForm() which drops the suffix

trace.note: if this.subnetMask (7) < address.subnetMask (8) return false
isHostInSubnet ignores the caller's own prefix and would return true
Address4.isInSubnet exposes the containment version under the same name
Address6.isInSubnet, same footgun

finding.guards_checked: The doc comments at common.ts:9-18 and ipv4.ts:457-465 warn to use isHostInSubnet for untrusted input. This is API misuse, not a flaw in the function's stated contract. Not executed.

finding.claim: embeddedIPv4() unwraps only IPv4-mapped and NAT64 well-known addresses. 6to4 (2002::/16) addresses that embed a private or loopback IPv4 are classified as public by isPrivate, isLoopback and related checks.
finding.sink: Trust-boundary classifier used as an SSRF deny-check on a host with 6to4 routing

trace.note: embeddedIPv4 checks isMapped4 and NAT64_WELL_KNOWN only
is6to4() exists but is not consulted by the trust-boundary classifiers
isPrivate() returns false for 2002:0a00:0001::, since ULA and NAT64 local-use do not match

finding.guards_checked: ULA and NAT64 local-use checks: not applicable. Exploitability depends on the host having a 6to4 relay or tunnel; not verified.

finding.claim: RE_ZONE_STRING /%.*$/ is quadratic on many % characters followed by a newline, so a long attacker-supplied address string can block the event loop.
finding.source: Untrusted string passed to new Address6() or Address6.isValid()/fromURL(), e.g. '%'.repeat(N) + '\n'
finding.sink: CPU time in the constructor before the bad-character check

trace.note: RE_ZONE_STRING.exec(address) runs on the full string with no length limit
/%.*$/: each % starts a scan to the newline, then backtracks, so the cost is O(n^2)

finding.guards_checked: RE_SUBNET_STRING is linear; the slash test runs first. No length cap in the constructor. Timing not measured; no execution tool was available.

finding.claim: href(optionalPort) concatenates a string port without validation, so a caller passing untrusted text can change the host and URL structure, e.g. '80@evil.example'.
finding.source: Caller-supplied port string (type number | string) taken from user input
finding.sink: Returned URL string used for a redirect or outbound fetch

trace.note: href(optionalPort?: number | string)
optionalPort is interpolated as ':${optionalPort}' with no escaping or numeric check
returns http://[correctForm]:<port>/

finding.guards_checked: Host part is safe (correctForm only emits hex and colons). Port is unchecked. Exploitability requires the caller to pass an untrusted string as the port.
